examples.claim: HTTP proxy: one on the head node by default; proxy_location in serve.start() or config for per-node proxies
examples.source: architecture.html: 'By default there is one HTTP proxy actor on the head node ... via the proxy_location field inside serve.start() or the config file.' (conflicts with production-guide/config.html 'EveryNode (default)', which the post states at L642)

examples.claim: power of two choices subject to max_ongoing_requests; handles poll the controller for new replicas
examples.source: architecture.html: 'Each DeploymentHandle continuously polls the controller ... power of two choices scheduling strategy, subject to the constraint that no replica is handling more than max_ongoing_requests'

examples.claim: request objects of 100KiB+ go via the object store with zero-copy read; smaller ones via network call
examples.source: architecture.html: 'Larger request objects (100KiB+) are written to the object store and the replica can read them via zero-copy read.'

examples.claim: controller data checkpointed to GCS on head node; transient router/replica queues lost on machine failure
examples.source: architecture.html: 'All data in the Controller ... is checkpointed to the Ray Global Control Store (GCS) on the head node. Transient data ... will be lost'

examples.claim: route_prefix default '/', must start with '/', cannot end with '/' unless it is '/', no wildcards; FastAPI routes layer on top
examples.source: http-guide.html 'routes ... layered on top of the route prefix'; schema.py _route_prefix_format rules 1-3

examples.claim: serve run blocks and streams logs, Ctrl-C shuts down Serve; with a YAML, unchanged apps are not updated
examples.source: serve run --help (Ray 2.60.0): 'If passing a YAML config, existing applications with no code changes will not be updated. By default, this will block ...'

examples.claim: application status is one of NOT_STARTED/DEPLOYING/RUNNING/DEPLOY_FAILED/DELETING; deployment status is three values HEALTHY/UNHEALTHY/UPDATING
examples.source: monitoring.html: 'A Serve deployment has six possible statuses' (UPDATING, HEALTHY, UNHEALTHY, DEPLOY_FAILED, UPSCALING, DOWNSCALING); schema ApplicationStatus also has UNHEALTHY

examples.claim: serve deploy --working-dir must be a remote .zip URI, not a local dir
examples.source: serve deploy --help: 'This must be a remote URI to a .zip file (e.g., S3 bucket) ... Ignored when deploying from a config file.' (the post's context is a config-file deploy, where the flag is ignored)

examples.claim: num_replicas='auto' equals max_ongoing_requests 5, target_ongoing_requests 2, min_replicas 1, max_replicas 100
examples.source: autoscaling-guide.html 'Setting num_replicas="auto" is equivalent to ...' block

examples.claim: over-limit HTTP requests get 503 by default; handle calls raise BackPressureError
examples.source: configure-serve-deployment.html: 'raise a BackPressureError (for handles) or return an HTTP 503 status code by default (configurable via backpressure_config)'

examples.claim: two Serve env vars govern proxy restart and draining
examples.source: production-guide/config.html lists four proxy env vars (HEALTH_CHECK_PERIOD_S 10.0, HEALTH_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S 10.0, READY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_S 5.0, MIN_DRAINING_PERIOD_S 30.0); the period var also sets the restart timing

examples.claim: during draining the proxy fails LB health checks; ongoing requests finish; min draining 30 s
examples.source: config.html RAY_SERVE_PROXY_MIN_DRAINING_PERIOD_S: '(1) the proxy fails health checks ... (2) ongoing requests complete normally ... Default is 30.0.'

examples.claim: Serve LLM usage data list (architecture, JSON mode, LoRA count, autoscaling min/max, TP size, initial replicas, GPU type/count); opt out via usage stats
